statement: Are there any integer solutions to x^x * y^y = z^z with x, y, z > 1?
status: solved (affirmative), Ko (Chao Ko) 1940; erdosproblems.com marks it PROVED (LEAN)
notes: RESOLVED IN THE AFFIRMATIVE: yes, solutions exist (Ko 1940 found infinitely many). Formalize the affirmative assertion: there exist natural numbers x, y, z all > 1 with x^x * y^y = z^z. WARNING for proving: any witness has astronomically large x^x, so `decide`/`norm_num` on the raw equation will never terminate — the proof must work with the structure of the witness (e.g. writing x, y, z as products of prime powers and comparing exponents via pow_mul / mul_pow style rewriting), reducing the equation to small linear identities on exponents.
